tasks.subject: Verify repo is a valid DSH plugin

Report: repo structure, package.json name/version, the dsh.bundle path and whether it exists, any other dsh plugin fields, and a loadability verdict.

tasks.subject: Install plugin via dsh plugin CLI
tasks.description: Run the DSH CLI install command: `dsh plugin --profile web add github:zouyuxuan122/Deepseek-Harness-EAC` (run from a suitable working dir; if the repo is an npm package published to npm, use the npm package name instead — first check `npm view <name>` for the package name found in step 1). tasks.subject: Verify installation result and restart requirement
tasks.description: After install, verify: (1) the plugin is registered at the bundle layer — inspect dsh's plugin registry/state (e.g. `dsh plugin --profile web list`, or check the profile config/plugins state files under the dsh data dir; use `dsh --dump-config` and any `dsh plugin list` subcommand). Confirm the plugin appears. (2) Confirm `--dump-config` output shows the plugin. (3) Determine whether the web profile needs a restart for the bundle to take effect — check if the bundle is injected at runtime startup (bundle registration is typically read at profile boot) vs hot-loaded. Report: evidence of registration (command outputs), whether --dump-config shows it, and a clear restart recommendation with reasoning.
